title: Perf thermostat scrub: small-seq p95 spike investigation
content:
Meeting: Weekly perf thermostat scrub (21 Apr 2026)
Owner: Ava Chen (notes)
Goal: Triage unexpected p95 spikes for small-sequence online traffic after kernel selection refactor. Capture reproducible runs, narrow hypothesis, assign owners and next steps.

Attendees:
- Ava Chen (notes)
- Marco Ruiz
- Priya Nair
- Ethan Park
- Lina Gomez (observability)

TL;DR:
- Observed p95 jump from ~48ms -> ~120ms for sequences <= 32 tokens on variety-a model after kernel selector v2 rolled on 2026-04-18. Bulk throughput largely unchanged. Regression appears load-shape dependent and correlated with frequent KV cache flushes.
- Repro steps and a minimal local harness were created (run id: thermostat-0421-r1). Repro is noisy but shows median p95 ~115ms across 10 repeats.
- Short-term mitigation: fallback to kernel-selector v1 for affected pods in the canary pool; rollout paused.

Observed signals and quick metrics:
- Canary cluster (region us-west-2) traffic window: 2026-04-18 03:00 - 06:00 UTC
- Small-seq qps: 220 -> 210 (no big drop)
- p50: 18ms -> 22ms
- p95: 48ms -> 118ms
- CPU on host: +5% (normal). GPU util: same. Cuda context switching counters: up by ~2.3x for affected processes (observability metric cuda.ctx_switches).
- KV cache churn metric (kv.cache.evictions/sec) spiked during the window (~3.8x baseline).

Reproduction summary (local harness):
- Command: ./bench/harness --model variety-a --seq 16 --batch-dist poisson --qps 200 --kv-cache-on --kernel-selector v2 --seed 20260421
- Harness run id: thermostat-0421-r1 (artifacts uploaded to s3://perf-playback/thermostat/thermostat-0421-r1.tar.gz)
- Results (10 runs): p95s = [112, 118, 121, 110, 116, 117, 125, 109, 114, 119] ms -> median 116ms.
- Same command with kernel-selector v1: median p95 50ms.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel-selector v2 picks a kernel path that triggers extra stream synchronizations for short sequences (scheduling overhead dominates).
2) KV cache flush path interacts with micro-batching heuristic, causing frequent offload/restore operations (I/O + cuda memcopies) on samples with low token count.
3) New heuristic changed padding/packing behaviour for small batches, increasing hook calls into memory manager.

Quick checks performed during meeting:
- Re-ran harness with kv-cache disabled: p95 dropped to ~56ms (supports hypothesis #2).
- Added extra logging around stream launch in the runtime: observed 1.7x more host->device memcopy calls per request on v2 path.
- Single-request profiling with NVTX shows extra cudaStreamSynchronize in the hot path right after kv cache restore.

Logs (abridged):
- runtime:kernel_selector: INFO selected path=v2.kv-restore-sync
- runtime:kv: DEBUG restore_shard id=0 size=2.3MB time=2.1ms
- runtime:cuda: DEBUG memcpy_htod start t=2300.23 end t=2303.35 (3.12ms)
- runtime:cuda: DEBUG stream_sync after_restore t=2303.36 (synchronous)

Immediate actions (owner + ETA):
- [Ava] Pause v2 on canary pool (done during meeting).
- [Marco] Open PR to add async restore variant guarded by feature flag + perf test (PR drafted: linked). ETA: 2026-04-24.
- [Priya] Wire up micro-benchmark that isolates kv-restore path with and without async flag, run on perf lab GPUs. ETA: 2026-04-23 (in progress).
- [Ethan] Add NVTX-marked flamegraphs and upload to perf artifacts for the 10-run corpus. ETA: 2026-04-22 (done).
- [Lina] Add alert that p95 for small-seq traffic > 80ms for 5m should auto-fail kernel-selector rollout. ETA: 2026-04-25.

Longer-term investigations:
- Verify whether packer/padder changes in model compilation are contributing; schedule a pairing session with compilation team (owner: Marco, target: week of 2026-04-27).
- Evaluate a lightweight async restore path vs batched restores and measure additional memory pressure.
- Add a continuous small-seq shadow-run job in perf CI that runs nightly on representative models and flags >20% p95 regressions.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does kv.cache.evictions spike in these windows for small-seq traffic? (traffic shape? memory fragmentation?)
- Is there any cross-talk from other processes on the same GPU (multiplexed tenancy) that increases stream syncs?
- Could scheduler decision be influenced by recent heuristics that consider transient seq-length distributions?

Notes to self / shorthand observations:
- reproduce locally but prefer perf lab GPU vs dev laptop (latency numbers differ small-seq).
- harness should pin --quantize-mode=fp16 to match canary.
- verify driver/kernel versions are identical between canary and perf-lab.

Meeting artifacts and quick refs:
- reproducer run: s3://perf-playback/thermostat/thermostat-0421-r1.tar.gz
- PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-7891

Next check-in: short sync Tue 2026-04-23 16:00 UTC to confirm micro-bench numbers and decide on v2 rollback duration.

Action log (summary):
- rollback v2 to canary: done (Ava)
- micro-bench harness uploaded: in progress (Priya)
- PR to add async restore flag: drafted (Marco)
- NVTX artifacts: uploaded (Ethan)
- rollout guard alert: todo (Lina)

End notes: kept the doc intentionally terse — this is a noisy, reproducing regression. If you pick this back up, start with the harness id thermostat-0421-r1 and the async restore flag branch in the draft PR.
